walkthroughs.body_html:
Water evaporates from stomata.

Cohesion between water molecules pulls a continuous column up the xylem from roots. The faster water leaves, the faster more is pulled up.

Increase by: light (opens stomata), warmth, wind, low humidity.

can give you a potometer graph and ask you to predict the effect of changing one factor.

Sugars move from source (leaves) to sink (roots, fruits) — translocation.

Phloem is alive — sieve tube elements with companion cells.

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
